successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the County of Maine 'returning the county to the crown' in 1481

ledger.x: 990: the County of Maine, at Le Mans, enters the record; Hugh III (c.
1051: Geoffrey Martel of Anjou takes Le Mans.
1064: Maine passes from the Angevins to William of Normandy as count.
1070: Le Mans throws out the Normans.
1092: Hugh V sells Maine to his cousin Elias I of La Flèche.
1110: Fulk V of Anjou takes Maine.
1481: Charles IV of Anjou, Count of Maine since 1472, dies on 10 December and his domains pass to Louis XI.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Maine
wars.outcome: William of Normandy invaded Maine in 1063 against Fulk IV of Anjou and controlled the county by the beginning of 1064.

wars.name: Norman attacks on Maine
wars.outcome: After the Le Mans revolt of 1069 and the expulsion of 1070, Norman attacks came in 1073, 1088, 1098 and 1099; Elias I was captured on 28 April 1098, besieged Le Mans in 1099 and with Fulk expelled the Norman garrison in 1100.

wars.name: English occupation of Maine
wars.outcome: After Verneuil (1424) the English occupied Maine and John of Lancaster took the ducal title; they held Le Mans until 1448 and Fresnay until 1449.

wars.name: Geoffrey Martel's war over Maine
wars.outcome: Geoffrey Martel took Mans in 1051; 'For the next several years, the war was centered in the County of Maine, with Duke William on the offensive', and he kept resisting in Maine until his death on 14 November 1060.

certainty.note: A feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's single outline; no page gives a boundary line.
